:::{#cor-cdf-derivative-density-ae}
#### A CDF has its density as derivative at all but finitely many points

If $X$ is a continuous random variable with CDF $\cdf$
and a density $f$ that is continuous at all but finitely many points,
then $\cdf$ is differentiable with $\cdf' = f$
at all but finitely many points.

:::

::: proof

At every point $t$ where $f$ is continuous,
@thm-cdf-derivative-is-density gives $\cdf'(t) = f(t)$,
and by assumption those are all but finitely many points.

:::
